key_insight: Adding hierarchy-aware training and pleural-line mask guidance improved lung ultrasound video classification, with anatomy-guided supervision giving the best overall performance and more focused attention.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help automate bedside assessment of pulmonary edema by better distinguishing healthy lungs, B-lines, consolidations, and mixed patterns in ultrasound videos.
method: Trained a deep learning model for 4-class lung ultrasound video classification.
Compared flat classification with hierarchy-aware learning strategies.
Added pleural line mask supervision to guide attention toward anatomically relevant regions.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 1,886 videos from 219 patients using patient-level five-fold cross-validation, and tested transfer on the external COVID-BLUeS dataset; mask-guided attention achieved the highest mean macro-F1 of 65.7%.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable pleural-line mask supervision and may vary across scanners, operators, and external datasets.
paper_title: Hierarchy-Aware and Anatomy-Guided Learning for Lung Ultrasound Video Classification
